tests.description: A submodule's GIT_DIR (.git/modules/<name>/) carries its own config and hooks. A pillager that filters .git/config but not the nested one writes an executable directive into the operator's output directory. This scenario demonstrates the write, not execution: git only reads that config once the submodule is wired up (working tree plus a .git gitfile), which a recovered tree does not have — verified by running git status against the recovered repository, where the payload does not fire. Treat it as a latent hazard and a policy gap, not a proven RCE.

disclosures.notes: Self-discovered by this benchmark; fixed in commit bdff7ee — `OriginRestrictedSession` refuses cross-origin 3xx redirects.

Self-discovered. add_folder's file branch checked the origin but not the .git/ anchor, so a listing could steer the crawl at any same-origin path; the directory branch did check it. Fixed by folding both branches into _resolve_href, which applies origin, anchor and per-segment checks once. Pinned by tests/test_listing_dialects.py.

Self-discovered. add_folder kept no visited set and no depth cap, so a bottomless listing recursed until the path exceeded the filesystem limit (observed: 131 requests, then an unhandled OSError). Fixed with a visited-URL set and _MAX_CRAWL_DEPTH; the same scenario now finishes in 38 requests. Pinned by tests/test_crawl_robustness.py.

Recovers .git/modules/<name>/config carrying core.fsmonitor into the operator's output directory. Latent, not proven execution: git honours that config only once the submodule is wired up, and `git status` against the recovered tree fires nothing.

Recovers .git/modules/<name>/config carrying core.fsmonitor into the operator's output directory. Latent, not proven execution: git honours that config only once the submodule is wired up, and `git status` against the recovered tree fires nothing.
188 requests against a bottomless one-entry-wide listing: recursion is bounded by nothing the tool controls.
188 requests against a bottomless one-entry-wide listing: recursion is bounded by nothing the tool controls.

Self-discovered. GitHacker had been scoring PASS on B1 without earning it: a doubled slash in the URL the benchmark passes made every listing-derived path fail the origin prefix check, so the crawler recovered nothing and the poisoned index was never installed. With the URL normalised the tool works, and `git checkout-index --all --force` then honoured the attacker's index entry '../../canary/PWNED_B1' — an arbitrary file write outside the output directory, with no traversal anywhere in a URL. Fixed by validating every index path with `git ls-files` before installing the downloaded index or materialising it.
